# Cow (Mario)

**Cow** (Japanese: ウシ, Hepburn: *Ushi*), also referred to as **Moo Moo** (Japanese: モーモー, Hepburn: *Mō Mō*), is a fictional species of bovine from Nintendo's *Mario* franchise. Originally appearing as background elements and obstacles in the *Mario Kart* series, they made their debut in *Mario Kart 64* (1996). Distinguished by their rounded appearance and association with farm-themed race tracks, the Cows have become a recurring fixture in the franchise's spin-off titles, including the *Mario Party* and *Yoshi* series.

In the 2025 video game *Mario Kart World* for the Nintendo Switch 2, a specific female Cow was introduced as a playable driver for the first time in the series' history. This inclusion garnered significant attention from video game journalists and fans, leading to the character becoming a breakout popularity trend on social media, while also sparking minor controversies regarding in-game mechanics and animal rights depictions.

## Concept and creation

### Design and naming
The design of the Cow in the *Mario* franchise is a stylized, cartoonish depiction of a real-world Holstein Friesian cattle. They are characterized by white bodies with black spots, beady eyes, small horns, and pink udders . In their original appearance in *Mario Kart 64* (1996), the Cows were simple, low-polygon models without accessories. Starting with *Mario Kart DS* (2005), their design was updated to include a blue collar with a hanging yellow bell .

For the release of *Mario Kart World* (2025), the playable Cow character was given a more distinct model to differentiate her from the standard obstacles. This design includes a nose ring and animations that allow for driving vehicles; while she typically walks on all four legs, she is depicted holding handlebars with her front hooves while driving .

The nomenclature for the species has varied throughout the franchise's history. In Japanese, they are referred to as *Ushi* (Cow) or *Mō Mō* (Moo Moo) . Western localizations have used both terms interchangeably. "Moo Moo" is frequently used in the names of courses (e.g., Moo Moo Farm, Moo Moo Meadows) and in guidebooks describing them as obstacles . However, the playable character introduced in *Mario Kart World* is explicitly named "Cow" on the character select screen .

### Development of playable character
The transition of the Cow from a background element to a playable character occurred during the development of *Mario Kart World*. According to art director Masaaki Ishikawa, the concept originated from a "silly sketch" drawn by a designer during the creation of a ranch-themed area . The sketch depicted a cow driving a truck, which amused the development team.

Producer Kosuke Yabuki noted that the team was looking for new character additions following the extensive roster of *Mario Kart 8 Deluxe* and felt that utilizing "NPC drivers" (non-playable characters turned drivers) would fit the game's theme of an interconnected world . The Cow was the first of these "NPC drivers" to be prototyped; her successful implementation led to the inclusion of other traditional enemies and obstacles, such as Cheep Cheep and Pokey, as playable racers .

## Characteristics

### Species behavior
In their role as course elements, Cows are generally portrayed as passive creatures. In *Mario Kart 64*, they remain stationary behind fences in the background . In *Mario Kart Wii* and subsequent titles featuring the "Moo Moo Meadows" track, they serve as dynamic obstacles. They wander across the track, acting as heavy barriers that cause players to flip over or spin out upon collision . They are often associated with the in-universe brand "Moo Moo Meadows Milk," which appears on sponsorship signage and delivery trucks throughout the series .

### Playable character
The playable Cow in *Mario Kart World* is classified as a heavyweight character, sharing statistics with characters such as Wario and Donkey Kong . Unlike the human and anthropomorphic characters in the game, the Cow does not have unlockable alternate costumes . Her character emblem is a stylized icon of a cow's face .

In terms of animation, the character maintains a quadrupedal stance when moving outside of a vehicle but adopts a driving posture where her front hooves operate the steering wheel or handlebars. Developers noted the humorous contrast between her realistic animal behavior and the act of driving .

## Appearances

### *Mario Kart* series
The Cows are most prominent in the *Mario Kart* series, appearing in almost every main installment since 1996.

* **Mario Kart 64** (1996): Cows debuted in the course "Moo Moo Farm" (Mushroom Cup). They appear as 2D sprites and low-poly models in the background and do not interact with the racers .
* **Mario Kart: Double Dash!!** (2003): While physical Cows do not appear on tracks, they are featured on the side of passing trucks in the "Mushroom City" course, advertising Moo Moo Farm .
* **Mario Kart DS** (2005): The "Moo Moo Farm" course returns as a retro track. The Cows in the background were updated with 3D models featuring bells on their collars .
* **Mario Kart Wii** (2008): Cows appear as active obstacles in the "Moo Moo Meadows" course. They wander onto the track during the second and third laps, creating hazards for players .
* **Mario Kart 7** (2011): Cows appear on signage for "Moo Moo Dairy" in the "Coconut Mall" course .
* **Mario Kart 8** / **Mario Kart 8 Deluxe** (2014/2017): "Moo Moo Meadows" returns as a retro course with high-definition graphics. The Cows appear in multiple color variations, including brown and black spots . A Mii Racing Suit based on the Cow design was added via the *Booster Course Pass* .
* **Mario Kart Tour** (2019): The game features a "Moo Moo Offroader" kart and the Cow-themed Mii Racing Suit .
* **Mario Kart World** (2025): Released on June 5, 2025, for the Nintendo Switch 2, this title marks the first playable appearance of the Cow . The character was unlocked in version 1.0.0 but was made available from the start in subsequent updates . The course "Moo Moo Meadows" returns again, featuring a golden statue of a cow riding a bike .

### Other video games
Outside of racing, Cows appear in various sub-series of the *Mario* franchise.

* **Mario Party series**: Cows appear as background elements in the "Western Land" board in *Mario Party 2* (1999) and its remake in *Super Mario Party Jamboree* (2024) . They also appear in the "Fowl Play" minigame in *Mario Party 3* (2000) and on the "Perilous Palace Path" board in *Mario Party: Island Tour* (2013) .
* **Yoshi series**: In *Yoshi's Woolly World* (2015), a "Moo Moo Yoshi" pattern is unlockable . In *Yoshi's Crafted World* (2019), Cows appear as cardboard crafts and a wearable costume for Yoshi .
* **Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games**: Cows appear in the "Dream Equestrian" event, which is set in Moo Moo Meadows .
* **Minecraft**: The *Super Mario Mash-Up Pack* replaces the standard *Minecraft* cows with the *Mario* franchise design .
* **Mario Pinball Land**: A Cow makes a rare appearance as an interactive element .

## Reception

### Critical response
The Cows have generally been received as a charming, albeit minor, element of the *Mario* franchise's aesthetic. Their role as obstacles in *Mario Kart Wii* was noted for adding a dynamic, chaotic element to the racing experience .

The announcement and release of the Cow as a playable character in *Mario Kart World* in 2025 resulted in a surge of media coverage. *GameSpot* described the Cow as the "early breakout character" of the game, noting that fans immediately gravitated toward the absurdity of a farm animal driving a kart . *The New York Times* writer Rylee Kirk attributed the character's popularity to the "status elevation" from a background prop to a protagonist .

### Internet popularity
Following the April 2025 Nintendo Direct that revealed the character, the Cow became a subject of internet memes and fan art. On platforms such as TikTok and Instagram, gameplay clips of the Cow were frequently paired with the song "Mooo!" by Doja Cat . Fans also created edits of previous *Mario Kart* track thumbnails, inserting the Cow into various scenarios, such as a *Mad Max*-themed edit of Moo Moo Meadows .

### Controversies
The inclusion of the Cow in *Mario Kart World* sparked minor controversies. The animal rights organization PETA (People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals), which has previously criticized the *Mario* franchise for its depiction of the Tanooki Suit, issued a statement regarding the Cow. The group expressed concern over the character's ability to consume "Dash Food" items that resemble beef burgers, labeling it as a depiction of cannibalism .

This "cannibalism" theory became a topic of discussion among players and critics. Some fans argued that the food items were likely vegetarian substitutes, while others embraced the dark humor of the situation . When asked about the theory in an interview, producer Kosuke Yabuki declined to clarify the specific ingredients of the in-game food, stating only that the team was "happy with [the Cow's] reception" .

Everyone Keeps Picking Cow In Mario Kart World, Of Course
=========================================================

Cow is the early breakout character for Mario Kart World, and that's the udder truth.

By [Blair Marnell](https://www.gamespot.com/profile/blairmarnell/) on June 6, 2025 at 9:59AM PDT

[1 Comments](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/everyone-keeps-picking-cow-in-mario-kart-world-of-course/1100-6532182/#comments-block-33635915)

Where to buy

[Mario Kart World](https://www.gamespot.com/games/mario-kart-world/)

There are currently no available deals

GameSpot may get a commission from retail offers.

  

Cows or Moo Moos have been a part of the Mario Kart franchise since 1996's Mario Kart 64. However, [Mario Kart World](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/mario-kart-world-isnt-titled-mario-kart-9-because-nintendo-wants-to-take-the-series-to-the-next-level/1100-6531709/)\--one of the launch titles for [Switch 2](https://www.gamespot.com/gallery/best-nintendo-switch-2-games/2900-6618/)\--is the first game in the series to feature a cow behind the wheel. And fans seem to love playing as Cow online.

Images and videos of players picking Cow have been shared all over social media (via [Polygon](https://www.polygon.com/nintendo-switch-2/604129/mario-kart-world-cow-meme?taid=6841c615d752a100010a4204)) since Mario Kart World debuted earlier this week.

> 新作マリオカート、ウシ大人気でマジ草[#マリオカートワールド](https://twitter.com/hashtag/%E3%83%9E%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AA%E3%82%AB%E3%83%BC%E3%83%88%E3%83%AF%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB%E3%83%89?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/My1dGFS0UU](https://t.co/My1dGFS0UU)

> God, never in my whole life that I had lot of fun with Mario Kart World 🫶🏻 10/10 for me. Also, COW MAINS RISE UP MOOO 🐄 [pic.twitter.com/GRynbFwpKI](https://t.co/GRynbFwpKI)
> 
> — Ryan (@Clawspls1) [June 5, 2025](https://twitter.com/Clawspls1/status/1930766472357220540?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

> Anyone else’s online lobbies look like this in Mario Kart World? I’ve been in 3 full cow races [https://t.co/3EW1KwuYjh](https://t.co/3EW1KwuYjh)
> 
> — PhillyBeatzU | BeatzGames (@PhillyBeatzU) [June 5, 2025](https://twitter.com/PhillyBeatzU/status/1930775494116438512?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

> The first guy to post a montage of the Moo Moo Meadows Cow winning races in Mario Kart World Tour to the song La Vaca by Mala fe, Is getting the Latino pass at the Carne Asada [pic.twitter.com/kqd2chdfVc](https://t.co/kqd2chdfVc)
> 
> — Vance (@vancedotexe) [June 6, 2025](https://twitter.com/vancedotexe/status/1930975980065362144?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

In retrospect, this shouldn't be too surprising. There was an inordinate amount of interest in Cow after she was first spotted in the Mario Kart World teaser. Art director Masaaki Ishikawa subsequently revealed that the decision to turn Cow into a playable character [came from a silly drawing](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/how-a-silly-sketch-led-to-cow-becoming-a-pivotal-character-in-mario-kart-world/1100-6531712/) one of his colleagues made while working on the game.

The Cow can [eat burgers in MKW](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/mario-kart-worlds-cow-can-eat-burgers-and-steak/1100-6530642/), and she even hilariously seems to love it. That's led some to call her a cannibal, while others suggest that she's been eating a vegetarian meat substitute rather than consuming her own kind. Both of those theories may be overthinking the character a little bit.

Producer Kosuke Yabuki has acknowledged that Nintendo completely [underestimated Cow's popularity](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/mario-kart-worlds-cow-is-a-bigger-hit-than-nintendo-imagined-may-not-be-a-cannibal/1100-6532020/), but the company is happy with her reception. He also declined to weigh in about the cannibal or vegetarian theories.

Mario Kart World is out now on Switch 2, and you can keep picking Cow as long as you want to.

["This Is It!" - Nintendo On Why It Added 'Cow' Into Mario Kart World](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/05/news/2025/05/this-is-it-nintendo-on-why-it-added-cow-into-mario-kart-world)
============================================================================================================================================================================================

What an udder surprise

*   ![Image 2: Olliemar28](https://images.nintendolife.com/users/61767/avatar.jpg?v=1687185714)
*   by [Ollie Reynolds](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/05/authors/Olliemar28) Wed 21st May 2025

*   Share:
*   79
*   [](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/05/this-is-it-nintendo-on-why-it-added-cow-into-mario-kart-world# "Share this on WhatsApp")

[![Image 3: MK World - Cow 2](https://images.nintendolife.com/5686ba9dfd94f/mk-world-cow-2.900x.jpg)](https://images.nintendolife.com/5686ba9dfd94f/mk-world-cow-2.large.jpg "MK World - Cow 2")

_Image: Nintendo_

If you watched any of the reactions to the [Mario Kart World](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/05/games/nintendo-switch-2/mario-kart-world) reveal trailer, then chances are you saw somebody loudly exclaim "you can play as a _COW?!"_.

Yes, the cow, an NPC character known for its presence in Moo Moo Meadows, is now playable in the upcoming Mario Kart tile for Switch 2. In the recent [Ask the Developer](https://www.nintendo.com/us/whatsnew/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-3/) interview over at Nintendo, Masaaki Ishikawa explained the reasoning behind Cow's inclusion.

Honestly, it seems to have simply been a case of pondering what new additions could be added after Mario Kart 8 Deluxe included so many newcomers. Here's what Ishikawa had to say:

> "Each new _Mario Kart_ game features new characters to race with, but since we added so many to the previous game, we wondered where we could go from there. And then one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along, and I thought to myself, “This is it!” (Laughs) So that's when we realized the course surroundings actually contained a lot of untapped resources.
> 
> "The character designer quickly put together a prototype of Cow that could race, and surprisingly it didn't feel out of place at all. So we thought maybe we could include other obstacle characters, and decided to add Cheep Cheep and Pokey as racers. As a result, the idea of taking obstacle characters, usually found in courses in past games, and having them participate in races made sense to me in terms of an interconnected world."

Characters such as Cow and Cheep Cheep are known as 'NPC Racers' within Nintendo, with Ishikawa joking that Cow in particular "is actually a pivotal character in the Mario Kart series".

To coincide with the information from the Ask the Developer interview, Nintendo has also released new footage from Mario Kart World showcasing Cow taking part in one of the game's missions, as shown by [TodayNews on BlueSky.](https://bsky.app/profile/today.oatmealdome.me/post/3lpousecsiy2c) The task? "Mooove" through a herd of cows, of course. Chortle!

> 📰 \[Mario Kart™ World\] P Switch Mission #1 View this content in the Nintendo Today! app: 🔗 today.oatmealdome.me

| Cow |
| --- |
| [![Image 1: Rendered model of the black-and-white Moo Moo obstacle in Mario Kart 8.](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/5/52/MK8_Asset_Model_Moo_Moo_%28White%29.png/190px-MK8_Asset_Model_Moo_Moo_%28White%29.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MK8_Asset_Model_Moo_Moo_/(White/).png)  
Model from _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ |
| **First appearance** | _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_64 "Mario Kart 64")_ ([1996](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_games_by_date#1996 "List of games by date")) |
| **Latest appearance** | _[Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Party_Jamboree_%E2%80%93_Nintendo_Switch_2_Edition_%2B_Jamboree_TV "Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV")_ ([2025](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_games_by_date#2025 "List of games by date")) |

**Cows** (also referred to as **Moo Moos**)[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMoo-1)[\[2\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMooTwo-2) appear as a recurring species in the [_Super Mario_ franchise](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(franchise/) "Super Mario (franchise)"), first appearing in _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_64 "Mario Kart 64")_. They are primarily associated with farm-based courses in the _[Mario Kart](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart "Mario Kart")_ series, in which they typically act as obstacles.

History\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")\]
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### _Mario Kart_ series\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mario Kart series")\]

#### _Mario Kart 64_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mario Kart 64")\]

[![Image 2: Moo Moo Farm from Mario Kart 64.](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/e/e3/Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png/200px-Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png)

Cows can be seen in the background of the _Mario Kart 64_ course [Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm").

#### _Mario Kart: Double Dash!!_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mario Kart: Double Dash!!")\]

Although cows themselves do not appear in _[Mario Kart: Double Dash!!](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart:_Double_Dash!! "Mario Kart: Double Dash!!")_, [Mushroom City](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mushroom_City "Mushroom City") has a truck advertising the Moo Moo Farm course with the image of a cow.

#### _Mario Kart DS_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Mario Kart DS")\]

In _[Mario Kart DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_DS "Mario Kart DS")_, cows once again appear in the background of [N64 Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm"). It is the first game to give them the blue collars with hanging golden bells.

#### _Mario Kart Wii_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Mario Kart Wii")\]

[![Image 3: A cow in MKW](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/6/60/MushroomCow.png/140px-MushroomCow.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MushroomCow.png)

A Moo Moo as seen in _Mario Kart Wii_

In _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_, cows serve as obstacles in the course [Moo Moo Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows "Moo Moo Meadows"). When hit, they cause the player to spin out. While the ones seen up close use full models, some in the distant background reuse flat textures from _Mario Kart DS_. A truck in the [Moonview Highway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moonview_Highway "Moonview Highway") course also has a picture of a cow printed on it with the text "[Moo Moo Dairy](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_brands_debuting_in_Mario_Kart_Wii#Moo_Moo_Dairy "List of brands debuting in Mario Kart Wii")".

#### _Mario Kart 7_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Mario Kart 7")\]

Two cows make a small appearance in _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_ on a sign in the [Wii Coconut Mall](https://www.mariowiki.com/Coconut_Mall "Coconut Mall") course, which reads "Moo Moo Dairy".

#### _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Mario Kart 8 / Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")\]

Moo Moos return in _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ with the return of the Moo Moo Meadows track, with some Moo Moos now having other colors, such as solid black or brown. Also, in [Toad Harbor](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad_Harbor "Toad Harbor") and the game's rendition of [Toad's Turnpike](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad%27s_Turnpike "Toad's Turnpike"), there are advertising trucks and signs with Moo Moos on them. There is also a sponsor known as [Moo Moo Meadows Milk](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_brands_debuting_in_Mario_Kart_8_and_Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe#Moo_Moo_Meadows_Milk "List of brands debuting in Mario Kart 8 and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe"). In this game, Moo Moos appear in four different colors; white with blue spots, white with brown spots, black, or brown. The Mii Racing Suit based on a Moo Moo appears in the _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe_%E2%80%93_Booster_Course_Pass "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass")_.

#### _Mario Kart Tour_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mario Kart Tour")\]

[![Image 4: The Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit from Mario Kart Tour](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/c/c0/MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png/60px-MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png)

Although Moo Moos themselves do not appear in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_, the Moo Moo Meadows Milk sponsor returns in several courses in the game, and the [Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii "Mii") and [Moo Moo Offroader](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Offroader "Moo Moo Offroader") are both based on them and were introduced in the [Animal Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Animal_Tour "Animal Tour").

#### _Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")\]

In _[Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Live:_Home_Circuit "Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")_, the [Windmill Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Windmill_Meadows "Windmill Meadows") features some Moo Moos as obstacles.

#### _Mario Kart World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Mario Kart World")\]

[![Image 5: Cow in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/3/37/MKWMooMoo.jpg/200px-MKWMooMoo.jpg)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWMooMoo.jpg)

Cow racing in _Mario Kart World_.

In _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_, cows return as obstacles on Moo Moo Meadows. In addition, a cow appears as a playable character for the first time in the _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(franchise/) "Super Mario (franchise)")_ franchise as a whole. Her [emblem](https://www.mariowiki.com/Emblem "Emblem") consists of a stylized depiction of her face. Moo Moo Meadows also now features a large golden statue of a cow on a bike.

The playable cow is unlockable in version 1.0.0, but made available from the start following a software update. She is a heavyweight character, sharing statistics with [Wario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario "Wario"), [Waluigi](https://www.mariowiki.com/Waluigi "Waluigi"), [Donkey Kong](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong "Donkey Kong"), [Wiggler](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wiggler "Wiggler"), [Chargin' Chuck](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chargin%27_Chuck "Chargin' Chuck"), and [Pianta](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pianta "Pianta").

### _Mario Party_ series\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Mario Party series")\]

Moo Moos make four background appearances in the [_Mario Party_ series](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_/(series/) "Mario Party (series)"). They appear in the background of [Western Land](https://www.mariowiki.com/Western_Land "Western Land") in _[Mario Party 2](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_2 "Mario Party 2")_ and _[Super Mario Party Jamboree](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Party_Jamboree "Super Mario Party Jamboree")_ and [Fowl Play](https://www.mariowiki.com/Fowl_Play "Fowl Play") in _[Mario Party 3](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_3 "Mario Party 3")_, and in _[Mario Party: Island Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party:_Island_Tour "Mario Party: Island Tour")_, they appear on [Perilous Palace Path](https://www.mariowiki.com/Perilous_Palace_Path "Perilous Palace Path").

### _Mario Pinball Land_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Mario Pinball Land")\]

In _[Mario Pinball Land](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Pinball_Land "Mario Pinball Land")_, there is a rare chance for a Moo Moo to pop out of a hole by hitting a [Monty Mole](https://www.mariowiki.com/Monty_Mole "Monty Mole"). If [Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario "Mario") hits the Moo Moo before it disappears, he gains 100,000 [points](https://www.mariowiki.com/Point "Point").

### _Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games")\]

Cows reappear in _[Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_%26_Sonic_at_the_London_2012_Olympic_Games_/(Wii/) "Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games (Wii)")_ on Moo Moo Meadows as obstacles in the [Dream Equestrian](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dream_Equestrian "Dream Equestrian") event.

### _Yoshi_ series\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Yoshi series")\]

#### _Yoshi's Woolly World_ / _Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Yoshi's Woolly World / Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World")\]

Although Moo Moos themselves do not appear in _[Yoshi's Woolly World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "Yoshi's Woolly World")_ and _[Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Poochy_%26_Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World")_, Moo Moo Yoshi is available as an unlockable Yoshi [pattern](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Yoshi_designs_in_Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "List of Yoshi designs in Yoshi's Woolly World") which resembles a Moo Moo.

#### _Yoshi's Crafted World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Yoshi's Crafted World")\]

In _[Yoshi's Crafted World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "Yoshi's Crafted World")_, the Moo Moo Meadows Milk sponsor from _Mario Kart 8_ makes various cameo appearances on the cartons and signs in the background of the flip side of [Rail-Yard Run](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rail-Yard_Run "Rail-Yard Run") and [Go-Go Yoshi](https://www.mariowiki.com/Go-Go_Yoshi "Go-Go Yoshi"). As first seen on the front side of Rail-Yard Run, there are also five cardboard Cow [crafts](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_crafts_in_Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "List of crafts in Yoshi's Crafted World"), which serve as [Coal Blockafeller](https://www.mariowiki.com/Blockafeller "Blockafeller")'s first souvenir request. There is additionally a Cow [costume](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_costumes_in_Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "List of costumes in Yoshi's Crafted World") for Yoshi to wear.

### Other appearances\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Other appearances")\]

#### _Nintendo Badge Arcade_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Nintendo Badge Arcade")\]

Cows[\[3\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-badge-3) appear as badges in _[Nintendo Badge Arcade](https://www.mariowiki.com/Nintendo_Badge_Arcade "Nintendo Badge Arcade")_ that the player may collect and decorate their Nintendo 3DS HOME Menu with. They are a part of the _Mario Kart 8_ set of badges.

#### _Minecraft_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Minecraft")\]

In the Super Mario Mash-Up Pack in _[Minecraft](https://www.mariowiki.com/Minecraft "Minecraft")_, the traditional [Cow](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Cow "minecraftwiki:Cow")'s design is replaced with the Moo Moo design found in the _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(franchise/) "Super Mario (franchise)")_ titles. Red and green Moo Moos with mushrooms on their back replace Mooshrooms.

Naming\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Naming")\]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The name "Cow" (capitalized as such) is used in-game in _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_. Prior to this, supplementary material variously referred to them as "cows" (in lowercase)[\[4\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-switch-4)[\[5\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-7)[\[3\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-badge-3) or "Moo Moos"[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMoo-1)[\[2\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMooTwo-2) (alternatively lowercased as "moo moos"),[\[4\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-switch-4) with the latter being primarily used by third-party guidebooks. Though the name "Moo Moo" has never been explicitly used to refer to them in-game, it is implied in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ by the name of the Moo Moo [Mii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii "Mii") Racing Suit.

| | **Moo Moo Meadows** is the second race course of the [Mushroom Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mushroom_Cup "Mushroom Cup") in _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_. The course is inspired by and serves as a successor to the _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_64 "Mario Kart 64")_ track [Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm"). An arrangement of Moo Moo Meadows' music is heard in the second half of the credits music along with [Luigi Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Luigi_Circuit_/(Mario_Kart_Wii/) "Luigi Circuit (Mario Kart Wii)")/[Mario Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Circuit_/(Mario_Kart_Wii/) "Mario Circuit (Mario Kart Wii)") and [Maple Treeway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Maple_Treeway "Maple Treeway"). The course returns as a [classic course](https://www.mariowiki.com/Classic_course "Classic course") in _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ where it is the first course of the [Shell Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Shell_Cup "Shell Cup"), and in _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_ as the first course of the [Lightning Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lightning_Cup "Lightning Cup"). In both _World_ and the original version of _8_, it is also used in [Battle Mode](https://www.mariowiki.com/Battle_Mode "Battle Mode"). Battle Mode in _8_ does not change Moo Moo Meadows' layout at all, while in _World_ multiple pathways are opened up in the middle. In _[Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Live:_Home_Circuit "Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")_, a similar course known as [Windmill Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Windmill_Meadows "Windmill Meadows"), which reuses the _Mario Kart 8_ version of its music, was added in the version 2.0.0 update. _Mario Kart Wii_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Mario Kart Wii")\] -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ### Course layout\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Course layout")\] [![Image 25: Wii Moo Moo Meadows from Mario Kart Wii](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/8/88/MKWii-MooMooMeadows2.png/200px-MKWii-MooMooMeadows2.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWii-MooMooMeadows2.png) The course is located in a rural area of green hills, with a river near a farm, and a few trees surrounding the track. The scenery around the track includes a milk cart, a barn, a windmill, a river with a bridge and some dirty paths leading to outside the meadows. At the start of the track, there is a brief straightaway and then a gradual turn left, passing a farm with a silo. About halfway through this turn is the first set of [Item Boxes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Item_Box "Item Box"). Then, there is another turn to the left leading the racer into the meadows where several [Moo Moos](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") are grazing. On the first lap, they stay to the side of the road, but on the other laps, the Moo Moos cross the road, serving as obstacles for the players. If one happens to run into a Moo Moo, they flip over and lose their item. There are two herds of Moo Moos - one in the middle area of the meadow, and the other one in the turn exiting it. After racers serpentine through the meadow, they encounter the second item set followed by a slight right turn and a simple blue ramp. After the ramp, there is a left turn where racers will encounter the first of several [Monty Moles](https://www.mariowiki.com/Monty_Mole "Monty Mole"). The Monty Moles will burrow around the track, leaving behind dirt trails that slow racers down, before stopping and trying to pop out of the ground to hit racers. After the left turn, racers enter an open area with multiple routes; several small grassy hills lie throughout the track and racers must weave around them, though there is a [dash panel](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dash_Panel "Dash Panel") ramp that allows them to jump over the first hill. The last item set can be found here; there are Item Boxes both floating in midair above the hill, and to the left and right of the hill. Several more Monty Moles are also found around the hills. After this section, there is a slight left turn and racers then reach the finish line. Moo Moo Meadows is one of two courses in _Mario Kart Wii_, along with [SNES Ghost Valley 2](https://www.mariowiki.com/Ghost_Valley_2 "Ghost Valley 2"), that did not have an online tournament take place on it. ### Shortcuts\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: Shortcuts")\] The first notable set of shortcuts can be found in the meadow. Two of the turns can be cut off, each only requiring a single [Mushroom](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dash_Mushroom "Dash Mushroom"), but if the player has other speed items they can cross the entire meadow without needing to stay on the road. This can be especially beneficial when the Moo Moos are crossing the road itself. The second notable set of shortcuts can be found in the final section with the grassy hills; the player can use speed items to drive over the hills to save time and avoid being slowed down by the Monty Moles. _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Mario Kart 8 / Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")\] -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- [![Image 26: Wii Moo Moo Meadows in Mario Kart 8](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/8/8f/MK8_Wii_Moo_Moo_Meadows.png/250px-MK8_Wii_Moo_Moo_Meadows.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MK8_Wii_Moo_Moo_Meadows.png) Wii Moo Moo Meadows in _Mario Kart 8_ Moo Moo Meadows makes its classic course debut in _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ as the first course of the [Shell Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Shell_Cup "Shell Cup"). The course is also available in the [Battle Mode](https://www.mariowiki.com/Battle_Mode "Battle Mode") of the Wii U version of _Mario Kart 8_. Its layout is mostly retained but has several notable changes. The track as a whole is more varied and uneven in elevation. At the turn after the simple ramp, the outside of the turn has been elevated and ends in a [glide ramp](https://www.mariowiki.com/Glide_Ramp "Glide Ramp"). The hills at the ending section have also significantly been reduced in size, expanding the main track as a result. The Monty Moles no longer leave behind trails that slow down racers; instead, the trails can be used as ramps for racers to perform [tricks](https://www.mariowiki.com/Jump_Boost "Jump Boost") off of. Lastly, the first set of Item Boxes now appears at the start of the first turn, the last item set is removed altogether, and Double Item Boxes appear at the second item set in _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_. The course also has received several visual and auditory changes. The time of day has changed to morning, and a rooster can be heard crowing at the start of the course intro. There are now more farms, variations of Moo Moos, and windmills. The once-bobbing trees are now stationary trees. The start/finish line banner is now similar to the banner on [Thwomp Ruins](https://www.mariowiki.com/Thwomp_Ruins "Thwomp Ruins") and uses the modern _Mario Kart_ logo. The music is now orchestrated, using more fiddle in the theme. Based on a city map that can be found in [Super Bell Subway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Bell_Subway "Super Bell Subway"), Moo Moo Meadows is shown to be located on the outskirts area of the city that contains both [Toad Harbor](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad_Harbor "Toad Harbor") and [Wii Wario's Gold Mine](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario%27s_Gold_Mine "Wario's Gold Mine"), as well as the same city that [N64 Rainbow Road](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rainbow_Road_/(Mario_Kart_64/) "Rainbow Road (Mario Kart 64)") hovers over.[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows#cite_note-1) _Mario Kart World_\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Mario Kart World")\] ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ [![Image 27: Moo Moo Meadows in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/3/3c/MKWorldMooMooMeadows.png/200px-MKWorldMooMooMeadows.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorldMooMooMeadows.png) Moo Moo Meadows in _Mario Kart World_ Moo Moo Meadows returns in _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World "Mario Kart World")_, appearing as the first course of the [Lightning Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lightning_Cup "Lightning Cup"). This makes it the first course in the series' history to appear as a classic course twice in a row in the base game, as [SNES Rainbow Road](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rainbow_Road_/(Super_Mario_Kart/) "Rainbow Road (Super Mario Kart)"), [Wii Coconut Mall](https://www.mariowiki.com/Coconut_Mall "Coconut Mall"), [N64 Kalimari Desert](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kalimari_Desert "Kalimari Desert"), [DS Waluigi Pinball](https://www.mariowiki.com/Waluigi_Pinball_/(race_course/) "Waluigi Pinball (race course)"), [Wii Mushroom Gorge](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mushroom_Gorge "Mushroom Gorge"), [Wii Maple Treeway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Maple_Treeway "Maple Treeway"), [Wii Koopa Cape](https://www.mariowiki.com/Koopa_Cape "Koopa Cape"), and [GCN Daisy Cruiser](https://www.mariowiki.com/Daisy_Cruiser_/(race_course/) "Daisy Cruiser (race course)") were all in _Mario Kart 7_ but were DLC courses in their _Mario Kart 8_ reappearance. The course also appears as the third checkpoint of the [Golden Rally](https://www.mariowiki.com/Golden_Rally "Golden Rally"), the second checkpoint of the [Moon Rally](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moon_Rally "Moon Rally"), and the fourth checkpoint of the [Heart Rally](https://www.mariowiki.com/Heart_Rally "Heart Rally"). It is the first Mushroom Cup course to appear as a classic course in the Lightning Cup, and one of two overall alongside [Toad's Factory](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad%27s_Factory "Toad's Factory"). A barn with a giant statue of a [cow](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") driving a motorcycle has been added in the center of the course. [Kamek](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kamek_/(item/) "Kamek (item)") will turn racers into either [Cow](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") or [Para-Biddybud](https://www.mariowiki.com/Para-Biddybud "Para-Biddybud"). The course is also passed through in the [Special Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Special_Cup "Special Cup") between [Mario Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Circuit_/(Mario_Kart_World/) "Mario Circuit (Mario Kart World)") and [Peach Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach_Stadium "Peach Stadium"), making it one of the few courses to directly be part of a route between two other courses (another is [Koopa Troopa Beach](https://www.mariowiki.com/Koopa_Troopa_Beach_/(Super_Mario_Kart/) "Koopa Troopa Beach (Super Mario Kart)"), which is part of the route between [DK Spaceport](https://www.mariowiki.com/DK_Spaceport "DK Spaceport") and Peach Stadium). The course is very similar to its iteration from _Mario Kart 8_. A few more cows serve as obstacles, the track contains a few more hills outside of the grassy hills, and a shortcut ramp on the left-hand side replaces the ramp over the grassy hills. The music appears to be a hybrid of the _Mario Kart Wii_ and _Mario Kart 8_ arrangements, combining the emphasized beat of the former with the melody of the latter. Geographically, the course is located in the center of the map, in the middle of the grassy plains region. There is a sign stating that the farm has been in activity since 2008, referencing _Mario Kart Wii_'s release date. ### Battle\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Battle")\] The track also appears as a battle course, though unlike in the original _Mario Kart 8_, various routes have been added within the center of the track to make it a more traditional battle experience.[\[2\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows#cite_note-2) The paths that are opened up primarily lead to the barn with the Cow statue, which is also opened up. An arrangement of the theme for [Chain Chomp Wheel](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chain_Chomp_Wheel "Chain Chomp Wheel") from _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_ plays on this version of the course. ### Routes\[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows?action=edit§ion=7 "Edit section: Routes")\] There are four distinct paths that enter Moo Moo Meadows, depending on the route taken to reach the course. * Traveling from [Crown City](https://www.mariowiki.com/Crown_City "Crown City"), [Choco Mountain](https://www.mariowiki.com/Choco_Mountain "Choco Mountain"), or [Toad's Factory](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad%27s_Factory "Toad's Factory") enters the course from the final turn, behind the starting line. * Traveling from [DK Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/DK_Pass "DK Pass"), [Dandelion Depths](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dandelion_Depths "Dandelion Depths"), [Dry Bones Burnout](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dry_Bones_Burnout "Dry Bones Burnout"), or [Mario Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Circuit_/(Mario_Kart_World/) "Mario Circuit (Mario Kart World)") enters the course from the top, travelling through the barn in The course features [Kamek](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kamek "Kamek"), who tries to throws obstacles in the players' path, and a [Chain Chomp](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chain_Chomp "Chain Chomp") that appears before the conclusion of the event. A badge mentions Moo Moo Meadows directly in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_. The badge depicts a logo for Moo Moo Meadows Milk, and was added in the [2023 Mii Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii_Tour_/(2023/) "Mii Tour (2023)"). The Moo Moo Meadows logo also appears in [GCN Waluigi Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Waluigi_Stadium_/(Mario_Kart:_Double_Dash!!/) "Waluigi Stadium (Mario Kart: Double Dash!!)"). Nintendo Explains How The Cow Became A Playable Character In Mario Kart World

Nintendo Explains How The Cow Became A Playable Character In Mario Kart World
=============================================================================

##### [7 months ago](https://nintendosoup.com/nintendo-explains-how-the-cow-became-a-playable-character-in-mario-kart-world/ "7 months ago") [Iggy](https://nintendosoup.com/author/iggynosuupu/ "View all posts by Iggy") Comments [0 Comment](https://nintendosoup.com/nintendo-explains-how-the-cow-became-a-playable-character-in-mario-kart-world/#respond)

In the first developer interview for Mario Kart World, Nintendo developers shared how the Cow became a playable character in Mario Kart World.

When working on an early version of a course in the game, a sketch of a cow driving a kart came up. This led to character designer quickly putting together a prototype of Cow that could race, which didn’t feel out of place. Nintendo then later expanded the idea to other obstacle characters, such as Cheep Cheep and Pokey. Thanks to the addition of the obstacle drivers, the Kamek item was born, and more obstacle characters were turned into drivers as a result:

> **Now that you mention it, some of the new characters in this game seem like unlikely picks. I was surprised to see Cow as one of the playable characters.**
> 
> **Yabuki**: That’s right. In previous games in the series, Cow was part of the scenery or an obstacle on one of the courses. But when we were working on an early version of a course in this game set on a ranch that players can drive through, this sketch came up. (Laughs)
> 
> **Oh, I thought Cow was just on the back of the truck, but she’s actually driving it. (Laughs)**
> 
> **Ishikawa**: Each new _Mario Kart_ game features new characters to race with, but since we added so many to the previous game, we wondered where we could go from there. And then one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along, and I thought to myself, “This is it!” (Laughs) So that’s when we realized the course surroundings actually contained a lot of untapped resources.
> 
> The character designer quickly put together a prototype of Cow that could race, and surprisingly it didn’t feel out of place at all. So we thought maybe we could include other obstacle characters, and decided to add Cheep Cheep and Pokey as racers. As a result, the idea of taking obstacle characters, usually found in courses in past games, and having them participate in races made sense to me in terms of an interconnected world.
> 
> **Sato**: We called these types of characters “NPC drivers.” In other words, non-player character drivers.
> 
> **Yabuki**: So it was like, “They’re NPCs, but they’re playable? Which is it?” (Laughs) It’s pretty funny to see a four-legged Cow holding onto motorcycle handlebars with her front hooves.
> 
> **Ishikawa**: But when she jumps, she strikes a proper quadrupedal pose. So I’m pretty sure Cow is still in touch with her animal nature. (Laughs)
> 
> **Jikumaru**: It was thanks to the introduction of various “NPC drivers” that the idea to have Kamek appear as an item was born. When Kamek casts a spell, the racers are transformed into playable NPCs, so one by one they might all turn into Cow mid-race. I think it turned out to be a unique item that has never been seen before. In fact, Cow is a character who’s inspired a lot of different ideas, including obstacle characters like Camel and Giraffe.
> 
> **Ishikawa**: Cow is actually a pivotal character in the _Mario Kart_ series. (Laughs)
> 
> **Asahi**: On the other hand, when previously non-playable characters like Cow become playable, it means giving them new ways to express emotion, which must have been difficult for the voice lead. We were conscious of depicting the personalities and characteristics of “NPC drivers” in a way that doesn’t look inferior to classic characters like Mario. The voice team members went through a lot of trial and error in the pursuit of the ideal sound. In addition to more characters, this game also has a wider selection of vehicles for characters to drive, so it was a huge task to create engine sounds that matched the characteristics, such as the appearance and structure, of each vehicle. We tried out a lot of different sounds in our search for something ideal—we even used croaking frogs and beating drums. (Laughs)
> 
> **Sato**: There are a lot of vehicles in this game, too. Since the game is about racing around the world, we’ve included not only race karts, but also everyday vehicles. It must have been tough for the designers, as they had to not only design the body of the vehicle, but also consider how the tires would transform when drifting and how the vehicle would move when jumping.

What do you think? Let us know in the comments.

Initially teased during the Nintendo Switch 2's reveal trailer on January 16, 2025, the game was properly revealed during the Nintendo Switch 2 Direct presentation on April 2, 2025. It is the sixteenth entry in the _Mario Kart_ series, the first new _Mario Kart_ title since 2020's _[Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Live:_Home_Circuit "Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")_, as well as the first original flagship entry in the series for a console since 2014's _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_. It is also the first _Mario Kart_ game to be a launch title for its console. The game's roster marked the playable debut of many enemies from across the series, including [Cataquack](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cataquack "Cataquack"), [Swoop](https://www.mariowiki.com/Swoop "Swoop"), and [Conkdor](https://www.mariowiki.com/Conkdor "Conkdor"), among many more. Altogether, this game features the most brand new playable character additions to the _Mario Kart_ series to date. Two new in-game modes were also added: Knockout Tour and Free Roam. The art style of the game's characters has changed to further resemble 2D illustrations drawn by [Shigehisa Nakaue](https://www.mariowiki.com/Shigehisa_Nakaue "Shigehisa Nakaue"), much like the in-game look of _[Super Mario Bros. Wonder](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Bros._Wonder "Super Mario Bros. Wonder")_. The game was covered during the Nintendo Treehouse: Live events on April 3 and 4, 2025.[\[35\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-TreehouseDay1Pt1-35)[\[36\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-TreehouseDay2Pt1-36) A dedicated Nintendo Direct for the game titled the "_Mario Kart World_ Direct" broadcast on April 17, 2025 at 6:00 a.m. PT / 9:00 a.m. ET / 2:00 p.m. BST.[\[37\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-MKWDirect-37) _Mario Kart World_ will be one of the first two Nintendo-published games to be localized in Polish (the other being _[Donkey Kong Bananza](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong_Bananza "Donkey Kong Bananza")_), with support to be added in a free update in early 2026.[\[38\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-38) Gameplay -------- ### New features Races now have 24 racers, doubling from the 12 seen in _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_, _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_, and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_, tripling from the eight seen in the other entries, and quadrupling the six from the arcade series. Players receive points in racing as before, with some positions receiving the same number of points, making _Mario Kart World_ the first _Mario Kart_ game where racers who finished in different places received the same number of points since _[Mario Kart: Super Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart:_Super_Circuit "Mario Kart: Super Circuit")_, when 5th-8th place were all awarded zero points. Although [underwater driving](https://www.mariowiki.com/Underwater_driving "Underwater driving") (introduced in _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_) and [anti-gravity](https://www.mariowiki.com/Anti-gravity "Anti-gravity") (from _Mario Kart 8_ and _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_) do not return, gliding does, with [gliders](https://www.mariowiki.com/Glider "Glider") being replaced by retractable wings on the vehicles. When going over water, the wheels of all vehicles change into water skis, allowing them to float on the surface of the water. Both of these mechanics create a comparable vehicle system to _[Diddy Kong Racing](https://www.mariowiki.com/Diddy_Kong_Racing "Diddy Kong Racing")_ and _[Diddy Kong Racing DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Diddy_Kong_Racing_DS "Diddy Kong Racing DS")_. Many new mechanics are introduced in this game: when holding down the button after a [hop](https://www.mariowiki.com/Hop_/(move/) "Hop (move)") without turning, players can charge up a [Charge Jump](https://www.mariowiki.com/Charge_Jump "Charge Jump") instead of initiating a [drift](https://www.mariowiki.com/Drift "Drift"). After such a jump, the player is granted a small speed boost similar to a [Mini-Turbo](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mini-Turbo "Mini-Turbo"). The jumps can be charged, yielding blue, then yellow, then rainbow sparks, with longer charges granting a longer-lasting boost after landing, similarly to drifting. Vehicles now have the ability to [Wall Ride](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wall_Ride "Wall Ride") by [Jump Boosting](https://www.mariowiki.com/Jump_Boost "Jump Boost") or Charge Jumping onto walls, and [Rail Ride](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rail_Ride "Rail Ride") on [grindrails](https://www.mariowiki.com/Grindrail "Grindrail")\[[_conjectural_](https://www.mariowiki.com/MarioWiki:Conjectural_names "MarioWiki:Conjectural names")\] and other thin platforms to quickly charge up [Mini-Turbos](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mini-Turbo "Mini-Turbo"). A new [Rewind](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rewind "Rewind") feature has also been added, which allows the player to rewind their position back to where they were before. However, this feature does not rewind the other racers and can only be used in Free Roam or in solo races and Time Trials. Unlike previous installments, all of the courses in the game take place in a large, open world, connected via the newly introduced [routes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Route "Route"), which are long, non-looping tracks filled with various hazards that connect from one course to another during races. Players are able to enter large vehicles scattered around the world marked with question marks, and temporarily control them from the inside. The vehicles available to control are [cargo trucks](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cargo_truck "Cargo truck"), boats, helicopters, and [UFOs](https://www.mariowiki.com/UFO "UFO"). Visually, the game is the first entry in the series, and the first _Super Mario_ game overall, that can be played in resolutions higher than 1080p. ### Controls | Action(s) | | --- | | ![Image 46: Single Joy-Con Left Button](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/c/c6/Switch_JC_Left_Button.svg) | Game modes ---------- ### Grand Prix [![Image 72: The icon for the Grand Prix mode in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/c/ce/MKWorld_Grand_Prix_icon.png/50px-MKWorld_Grand_Prix_icon.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Grand_Prix_icon.png) Grand Prix returns as the main game mode from previous games, where the player races through four courses of a cup in a chosen engine class (50cc, 100cc, 150cc, or the unlockable Mirror Mode) to attain the most points, with higher placements yielding more points. However, the format of the Grand Prix has been changed significantly from previous games. Now, only the first race of a cup follows the traditional multiple-lap format. The last three races follow a sectioned format instead, with the first two sections (or more in certain cases) of the race taking place across [routes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Route "Route") that transition from the previous course to the next, while the final section consists of one lap of that next course. Initially, only seven out of the eight cups are available in Grand Prix. Once a trophy has been obtained in all of them, a cutscene will play showing the seven trophies appearing at [Acorn Heights](https://www.mariowiki.com/Acorn_Heights "Acorn Heights") and combining into the [Special Cup](https://www.mariowiki.com/Special_Cup "Special Cup") trophy. The trophy will then fly across the sky with a rainbow trail behind it, much to the surprise of some of the racers. The trophy will then fly towards the Crown Bridge and immediately upwards, where it materializes into Rainbow Road offscreen. The Special Cup will then be unlocked for play. Like in past games, the player is able to get up to three stars in addition to a trophy in a Grand Prix. Like _Mario Kart 8_, the stars are purely based on points, with the player getting all three stars by getting 60 points, which is done by getting first place in all four races. As officially confirmed by Nintendo in a "Thank you for playing!" email sent to players,[\[39\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-39) Mirror Mode is unlocked by: * Playing the first seven cups in Grand Prix on 150cc (Nintendo's email however, erroneously states that all eight cups must be played in Grand Prix before replaying the Special Cup) * Playing all eight rallies in Knockout Tour on 150cc (with clearing checkpoints being optional) * Completing 10 [P Switch missions](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Mario_Kart_World_missions "List of Mario Kart World missions") in Free Roam * Activating 10 [? Panels](https://www.mariowiki.com/%3F_Panel "? Panel") in Free Roam * Collecting 10 [Peach Medallions](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach_Medallion "Peach Medallion") in Free Roam * Only after all of the above have been completed, the player must finish the Special Cup on 150cc to unlock it, including replaying the Special Cup if it has already been completed. Once all of the criteria have been fulfilled, a cutscene will play where a rainbow-colored light will travel into the stained glass on [the castle](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach%27s_Castle "Peach's Castle") in [Peach Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach_Stadium "Peach Stadium"). After a flash of light, the design on the stained glass will appear mirrored, and Mario will notice that the "L" on Luigi's cap is mirrored as well, in which the two will then celebrate. Mirror Mode will then be unlocked. Unlike _Mario Kart 8_ and _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_, progress made on a cup in Mirror Mode counts it for other engine classes as well, a feature that only applied to 100cc and 150cc in the aforementioned two games. Due to the increased racer count, 7th, 8th and 9th place are not considered losing places. A normal background signifies losing results (no clapping, character(s) showing a sad expression) and music. | ### Knockout Tour [![Image 73: The icon for the Knockout Tour mode in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/c/c7/MKWorld_Knockout_Tour_icon.png/50px-MKWorld_Knockout_Tour_icon.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Knockout_Tour_icon.png) Knockout Tour is a new all-out battle mode where players race over consecutive courses and routes across the open world and are eliminated at a specific checkpoint if they are in the last four places. Unlike races, there are no breaks in between, as players who qualify for the next race will simply continue in it. Knockout Tour consists of [rallies](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rally_/(event/) "Rally (event)") rather than cups, with each of the eight rallies having six checkpoints within. The first five races take place on a continuous path of them, with each checkpoint eliminating the players that place in the bottom four of the group. For the final race, the last four players standing will race a lap around the final course. Like in Grand Prix, there are up to three stars that can be obtained in each rally. function the same as they have previously. Players drive through a selected course to complete it as fast as possible. Like in previous games, players can race against [ghost times](https://www.mariowiki.com/Ghost_/(Mario_Kart_series/) "Ghost (Mario Kart series)") set by other players online. Staff ghosts return under the same name prefixes as in _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_, those being "Nin★". Like with _Mario Kart Tour_, lap/section splits are no longer available on the results screen, and are only shown on the timer after each lap/section, with the final split never shown. ### VS Race [![Image 76: Icon of the "VS." mode in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/8/86/MKWorld_VS_icon.png/50px-MKWorld_VS_icon.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_VS_icon.png) VS Race allows up to four players to play together locally and eight players to play wireless with custom rules. The settings available in VS Race are: * **Class:** The engine class the races will be played in. * **Teams:** Determines whether races are played in teams or individually. Unlike previous games, it is now possible to play in three teams of eight racers each or four teams of six in addition to only two teams of 12. * **Items:** Sets the item balance, with "Normal" containing regular item balance and "Frantic" giving chaotic items more frequently. The version 1.2.0 update also added the "Mushrooms Only" option, which only gives Mushroom-based items. The version 1.4.0 update re-introduced "Custom Items" from _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_, allowing players to manually select which items appear, though unlike last time, items cannot be set for specific teams in team races. * **COM Difficulty:** Sets the difficulty of computer racers, with the available options being "Easy", "Normal", and "Hard", or "No COM", which removes all computer racers. The latter option was initially only available in multiplayer, but was made available for single player as well starting in version 1.2.0. * **Course Selection:** Determines how courses are selected: * "Open" allows the player to select any course, including whether to play with routes or not. * In "Connected", the first race is chosen similar to "Open", but after that, the player can only select from three courses that connect from the previous course, and the race will involve traversing the route to the next course. Occasionally, one to two of those options will be replaced by the option to play a track in the traditional lap-style. The player can also select a random course, which may pick from one of the previously given courses with routes, or select a random course without routes. * "Random" has racers playing on a random course, which will also randomly choose whether it is played with laps or routes. * **Race Count:** Select the number of races played. The player is able to select three, four, five, six, eight, 12, 16, or 32 races. Several of the routes in VS Race give the destination course unique layouts compared to Grand Prix, Knockout Tour, and Time Trials, such as reverse layouts, combined layouts, or completely new layouts. ### Battle [![Image 77: The Battle Mode icon of Mario Kart World.](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/4/49/MKWRLD_Battle_Mode_Icon.png/50px-MKWRLD_Battle_Mode_Icon.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWRLD_Battle_Mode_Icon.png) [Battle](https://www.mariowiki.com/Battle "Battle") modes return, though as in _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_ and _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_, there are only two battle modes to choose from: [Balloon Battle](https://www.mariowiki.com/Balloon_Battle "Balloon Battle") and [Coin Runners](https://www.mariowiki.com/Coin_Runners "Coin Runners"). The settings for Battle mode are similar to VS Race, but engine class cannot be set (as all battles are played in 50cc), only "Open" and "Random" are available in course selection, and the number of rounds has a maximum of eight, as opposed to the 32 races in VS Race. Additionally, when using "Custom Items", turning off every item causes the [Mushroom](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dash_Mushroom "Dash Mushroom") to automatically turn on, while turning off every item except for the [Blooper](https://www.mariowiki.com/Blooper "Blooper") and/or [Dash Food](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dash_Food "Dash Food") causes the [Green Shell](https://www.mariowiki.com/Green_Shell "Green Shell") to automatically turn on. Matches have a set three-minute timer present during battles, which is non-adjustable like in _Mario Kart Wii_. #### Balloon Battle [![Image 78: Icon of the Balloon Battle mode in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/1/18/MKWorld_Balloon_Battle_icon.png/50px-MKWorld_Balloon_Battle_icon.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Balloon_Battle_icon.png) Balloon Battle has been reverted back to the elimination/point hybrid system used in _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_, where players gain points by hitting other opponents, and all of the points they gained will be added to their total score if they survive until the end. Unlike _Mario Kart 8_, if the player loses all of their balloons, they are not only eliminated from the game, but their score is also nullified, meaning that they get last place and do not get any points for the round. Like in _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_, players start with five balloons rather than three like in other games. Defeated players do not continue being able to use items like in _Mario Kart 8_. In local and online multiplayer, players can instead continue watching their opponents play, much like if they get eliminated in Knockout Tour. #### Coin Runners [![Image 79: Icon of the Coin Runners mode in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/f/f3/MKWorld_Coin_Runners_icon.png/50px-MKWorld_Coin_Runners_icon.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Coin_Runners_icon.png) Coin Runners functions similarly its previous appearances, where the objective is to collect the most coins when time limit expires while avoiding getting hit which will cause the player to lose coins. However, similar to _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_'s version of Coin Runners, there is a limit to the number of coins the player can collect, that being 20. Once the time is up, the number of coins the player collected will be added to their total point tally. ### Online Play [![Image 80: The Online Play icon of Mario Kart World.](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/0/07/MKWRLD_Online_Icon.png/50px-MKWRLD_Online_Icon.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWRLD_Online_Icon.png) Online multiplayer returns from previous _Mario Kart_ games and allows one or two people to play with others over the Internet. Four modes are available, being Race, Knockout Tour, Battle, and Friends. Race, Knockout Tour, and Battle feature random match-ups with players from around the world. The player has a separate score (similar to [Versus Rating](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7#VR "Mario Kart 7") from previous titles) for each mode, starting with 3000 and gaining points for their performance in each race or battle. If playing with two players, the second player will not have a score kept. * In Race, course selection is based on the "Connected" option seen in VS Race. After all players in the room have chosen a course, one player's choice is selected at random along with a random engine class. * In Knockout Tour, a random rally in a random engine class is chosen and played. * In Battle, the player can select from one of three battle courses, after which a course, along with either Balloon Battle or Coin Runners, is selected at random. #### Friends The Friends mode allows the player(s) to create or join a room, or view their battle history with people in their friends list. When creating a friend room, the host is able to set the rules of the room, including whether the mode played is a VS Race, Knockout Tour, Balloon Battle, or Coin Runners. In the settings, players can determine how long they will wait on the Free Roam map between races/battles through the "intermission" setting, with the options being 10 seconds, one minute, or five minutes. Course selection in VS Race will initially appear like in worldwide matches. However, pressing ![Image 81: Plus Button](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/d/d9/Switch_Plus.svg) on the course selection screen will instead toggle the "Open" course selection screen seen in offline VS Race. In Knockout Tour and Battle, the player is able to select any rally or battle course respectively they want to play on, which will then be chosen randomly among the players' choices. In all online modes, players can roam the world before and between matches. Unlike in the offline Free Roam mode, P Switches do not appear in these free roam lobbies, though players can still collect ? Panels and Peach Medallions, which will count towards their own totals. Characters ---------- The game has a total of 50 racers, with 32 being available from the start and 18 being unlockable. Of the total racers, 30 return from past installments and 20 are new (labeled in **bold**), most of whom are also playable for the first time in a video game overall, excluding [Goomba](https://www.mariowiki.com/Goomba "Goomba"), [Piranha Plant](https://www.mariowiki.com/Piranha_Plant "Piranha Plant"), [Pianta](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pianta "Pianta"), [Spike](https://www.mariowiki.com/Spike "Spike"), and [Dolphin](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dolphin "Dolphin"), as well as [Cheep Cheep](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cheep_Cheep "Cheep Cheep") and [Coin Coffer](https://www.mariowiki.com/Coin_Coffer "Coin Coffer") if [captures](https://www.mariowiki.com/Capture "Capture") in _[Super Mario Odyssey](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Odyssey "Super Mario Odyssey")_ are counted, and [Sidestepper](https://www.mariowiki.com/Sidestepper "Sidestepper") if [Mystery Mushroom](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mystery_Mushroom "Mystery Mushroom") [costumes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Costume_Mario "Costume Mario") in _[Super Mario Maker](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Maker "Super Mario Maker")_ are counted. Additionally, [Nabbit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Nabbit "Nabbit"), [Hammer Bro](https://www.mariowiki.com/Hammer_Bro "Hammer Bro"), [Chargin' Chuck](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chargin%27_Chuck "Chargin' Chuck"), and [Monty Mole](https://www.mariowiki.com/Monty_Mole "Monty Mole") are playable for the first time in a console _Mario Kart_ game following their debuts in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_. Excluding arcade games and _[Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Live:_Home_Circuit "Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")_, this is the first game in the _Mario Kart_ series since the introduction of [Mii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii "Mii") characters on the [Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wii "Wii") to not feature them as playable characters. This is also the first game to feature [Donkey Kong](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong "Donkey Kong")'s 2025 redesign outside of profile icons. Twenty-six drivers in this game are part of a sub-category of drivers referred to as "NPC drivers"[\[52\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart3-52) during development. These consist of all twenty newcomers, as well as six returning characters: [Dry Bones](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dry_Bones "Dry Bones"), [Wiggler](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wiggler "Wiggler"), Hammer Bro, Chargin' Chuck, Nabbit, and Monty Mole. All appear in the game as either background characters, obstacles during races, or hazards in Free Roam. During races, the [Kamek](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kamek_/(item/) "Kamek (item)") item can transform drivers into various characters from this group, while in some cases many members of that species will appear on the race track. Unlike the main roster, NPC drivers lack any alternate outfits, with Dash Food only providing them with a speed boost. ### Default drivers * [![Image 82: Consuming Dash Food unlocks outfits for use anytime, and the type of food the player uses determines the outfit the character wears. [Karts](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kart "Kart"), [bikes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Bike "Bike"), and [ATVs](https://www.mariowiki.com/All-Terrain_Vehicle "All-Terrain Vehicle") all return in _Mario Kart World_, the latter two following their absence in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_. In the case of bikes, [standard bikes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Standard_bike_/(vehicle_class/) "Standard bike (vehicle class)") return while [sport bikes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Sport_bike_/(vehicle_class/) "Sport bike (vehicle class)") do not. Kart customization as seen in _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_ and _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ does not return, with the vehicles in this game instead sporting a unique wheel design, and some lacking wheels entirely in favor of [treads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuous_track "wikipedia:Continuous track") or [skis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ski "wikipedia:ski"). Like the aforementioned two games, however, vehicles are unlocked by collecting a certain number of coins. Despite ATVs returning, the [Standard ATV](https://www.mariowiki.com/Standard_ATV "Standard ATV") does not. The [Gold Standard](https://www.mariowiki.com/Gold_Standard "Gold Standard") from _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_, _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_, _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_, and _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_ does not return. Players can also customize vehicles with [stickers](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_stickers_in_Mario_Kart_World "List of stickers in Mario Kart World"), decals that can be earned by completing certain objectives and placed on a specific spot on their vehicle, indicated by a pair of checkered flags as depicted in the vehicle's selection icon. There are 1,056 stickers, 39 of which are available from the start. There are 40 vehicles in the game, including 23 karts, 11 bikes, and six ATVs, allowing for a total of 6,120 character-vehicle combinations. Vehicles returning from previous installments are marked with their corresponding game in parentheses. 11 vehicles (six karts, four bikes, and one ATV) are available from the start while the rest,
