Counting courses with multiple variants together, _Mario Kart World_ has 30 courses, 16 of which are [new](https://www.mariowiki.com/New_course "New course"), while 14 [return](https://www.mariowiki.com/Classic_course "Classic course") from previous entries. In addition to the 30 courses, there are 202 [routes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Route "Route") connecting them all. Routes cause a track to function similarly to sectioned courses, driving two to four sections to the track before playing one lap of the destination course. The 14 returning courses consist of one course that debuted in both _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_ and the _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe_%E2%80%93_Booster_Course_Pass "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass")_, two courses each from _[Super Mario Kart](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Kart "Super Mario Kart")_, _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_64 "Mario Kart 64")_, _[Mario Kart: Double Dash!!](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart:_Double_Dash!! "Mario Kart: Double Dash!!")_, _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_, and _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_, and three courses from _[Mario Kart DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_DS "Mario Kart DS")_. One of the courses from _Super Mario Kart_, [Mario Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Circuit_/(Mario_Kart_World/) "Mario Circuit (Mario Kart World)"), is a combined version of multiple courses from that game, which can be driven through individually from certain routes. No courses from either _[Mario Kart: Super Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart:_Super_Circuit "Mario Kart: Super Circuit")_ or _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ return, marking a series first for the former game, and the second instance for the latter game after _Mario Kart Tour_. This is the first _Mario Kart_ game since _Mario Kart Wii_ to not have a classic Rainbow Road and the first game where Mario Circuit is only present as a classic course. Two new courses, [Crown City](https://www.mariowiki.com/Crown_City "Crown City") and [Peach Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach_Stadium "Peach Stadium"), are used twice in Grand Prix with different layouts; when played without routes, Crown City combines both of its Grand Prix layouts (with its Shell Cup and third layouts being significantly cut and the former driven in reverse), while Peach Stadium exclusively uses its Special Cup layout. Certain routes may cause Peach Stadium's Shell Cup layout to be mirrored. [Shy Guy Bazaar](https://www.mariowiki.com/Shy_Guy_Bazaar "Shy Guy Bazaar") and the aforementioned Crown City have additional layouts exclusive to VS Races when approaching from certain routes; approaching Shy Guy Bazaar from [Wario Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario_Stadium_/(Mario_Kart_64/) "Wario Stadium (Mario Kart 64)") or [Airship Fortress](https://www.mariowiki.com/Airship_Fortress "Airship Fortress") will take players onto a layout featuring a palace with [Daisy](https://www.mariowiki.com/Daisy "Daisy")'s emblem adjacent to the bazaar, while Crown City has a third layout in the nearby water if approached from Peach Stadium (except in the [Ice Rally](https://www.mariowiki.com/Ice_Rally "Ice Rally")), as well as [Moo Moo Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows "Moo Moo Meadows"), or [Choco Mountain](https://www.mariowiki.com/Choco_Mountain "Choco Mountain"). [Peach Beach](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach_Beach "Peach Beach") returns as a lap-section hybrid course, with lap 1 taking place through the original layout, with a new layout for sections 2 and 3; all routes leading to Peach Beach only utilize the new sections. Certain routes to [Mario Bros. Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Bros._Circuit "Mario Bros. Circuit"), [Desert Hills](https://www.mariowiki.com/Desert_Hills "Desert Hills"), Wario Stadium, [DK Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/DK_Pass "DK Pass"), [Koopa Troopa Beach](https://www.mariowiki.com/Koopa_Troopa_Beach_/(Super_Mario_Kart/) "Koopa Troopa Beach (Super Mario Kart)"), and Moo Moo Meadows lead to the course being driven backwards, similarly to reverse courses from _Mario Kart Tour_; in these cases, the minimap for the destination course will be flipped upside-down (except for Desert Hills and Moo Moo Meadows in the case of their routes from Mario Bros. Circuit and Peach Stadium respectively). Unlike previous games having a set skybox for each course, each course in the game (except [Rainbow Road](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rainbow_Road_/(Mario_Kart_World/) "Rainbow Road (Mario Kart World)")) has four different skyboxes for sunrise, daytime, sunset, and nighttime, which may progress when driving through routes and laps. Classic courses in this game (marked with their origin game's prefix below) have been revamped to an even greater extent than that of _Mario Kart 8_, bearing even less resemblance to the original courses as they appeared in previous games. While most of the classic courses present had already appeared as such in previous games, [Wario Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario_Stadium_/(Mario_Kart_64/) "Wario Stadium (Mario Kart 64)"), [Sky-High Sundae](https://www.mariowiki.com/Sky-High_Sundae "Sky-High Sundae"), and [Toad's Factory](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad%27s_Factory "Toad's Factory") appear as classic courses for the first time in the series. Unlike in _Mario Kart 8_ and _Mario Kart Tour_, all classic courses use the modern _Mario Kart_ logo for their finish lines, regardless of what game they originated from. This is the first _Mario Kart_ game since _Mario Kart: Super Circuit_ to not have prefixes appended to the names of any of the classic race courses, and the first for battle courses since _Mario Kart DS_. While not playable as traditional race courses, seven more courses from _Super Mario Kart_ can be seen or visited in Free Roam or during routes, including [Ghost Valley 1](https://www.mariowiki.com/Ghost_Valley_1 "Ghost Valley 1"), [Ghost Valley 2](https://www.mariowiki.com/Ghost_Valley_2 "Ghost Valley 2"), and [Ghost Valley 3](https://www.mariowiki.com/Ghost_Valley_3 "Ghost Valley 3") at the entrance to [Boo Cinema](https://www.mariowiki.com/Boo_Cinema "Boo Cinema"), [Koopa Beach 1](https://www.mariowiki.com/Koopa_Beach_1 "Koopa Beach 1") next to [Koopa Beach 2](https://www.mariowiki.com/Koopa_Troopa_Beach_/(Super_Mario_Kart/) "Koopa Troopa Beach (Super Mario Kart)") (here known as "Koopa Troopa Beach"), [Choco Island 1](https://www.mariowiki.com/Choco_Island_1 "Choco Island 1") and [Choco Island 2](https://www.mariowiki.com/Choco_Island_2 "Choco Island 2") south-east and south-west of [Choco Mountain](https://www.mariowiki.com/Choco_Mountain "Choco Mountain") respectively, and [Vanilla Lake 1](https://www.mariowiki.com/Vanilla_Lake_1 "Vanilla Lake 1") (referred to in-game as simply "Vanilla Lake") in an icy canyon north-east of [Wario Shipyard](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario_Shipyard "Wario Shipyard"). These courses can be raced in [P Switch missions](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Mario_Kart_World_missions "List of Mario Kart World missions"), the titles of which refer to them as "tributes". If these are counted, then Koopa Beach 1 and Ghost Valley 3 increase the number of courses making their classic course debut to five. Courses with differing names between British English and American English (i.e. [Wario Shipyard](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario_Shipyard "Wario Shipyard")) once again use their respective name depending on the game's region, unlike in _Mario Kart Tour_. ### Grand Prix The cups are ordered slightly differently compared to previous entries; the Special Cup is the eighth and last cup in the game, rather than the fourth. Unlike previous games since _Mario Kart DS_, the cups are also not separated between new and classic courses and instead feature a varying amount of both types of courses, similar to _Mario Kart 8_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_'s DLC cups, making this the first _Mario Kart_ game to lack the distinction between cups, excluding _[Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Live:_Home_Circuit "Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")_. Apart from the rotating cups in _Mario Kart Tour_, this is the second _Mario Kart_ game after _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_ to have cups with multiple classic courses from the same game, as the [Flower](https://www.mariowiki.com/Flower_Cup "Flower Cup"), [Banana](https://www.mariowiki.com/Banana_Cup "Banana Cup"), and [Lightning](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lightning_Cup "Lightning Cup") Cups have two tracks from _Mario Kart DS_, _Mario Kart: Double Dash!!_, and _Mario Kart Wii_, respectively, and it is the first entry to have this distinction from launch. In Grand Prix, the first course in each cup is driven for three laps, while the remaining three utilize routes from the previous course. The backgrounds of the cup icons correspond to the region that some of the cup's courses are located in; for example, the Star Cup's icon has an icy background, as its courses are near or within the snow region. Unlike in _Mario Kart 7_ and _8_, Grand Prix rivals are based off of the cup the player is racing on, rather than the character they chose, and they will always use a specific vehicle. If the player is playing as the cup's rival character, however, then a random character will serve as the primary rival instead. Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach_Stadium "Peach Stadium")** | ### Battle courses _Mario Kart World_ features eight battle courses, six of which are named after and derived from race tracks. [Moo Moo Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows "Moo Moo Meadows") features a new layout compared to its appearance in _Mario Kart 8_'s Battle mode. Two battle courses are not named after race courses: [Big Donut](https://www.mariowiki.com/Big_Donut "Big Donut"), returning from _Mario Kart 64_, and [Chain Chomp Desert](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chain_Chomp_Desert "Chain Chomp Desert"), a new course that functionally combines [Thwomp Desert](https://www.mariowiki.com/Thwomp_Desert "Thwomp Desert") and [Chain Chomp Wheel](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chain_Chomp_Wheel "Chain Chomp Wheel") from _Mario Kart Wii_. The top row of battle courses function like the B variants of courses from _Mario Kart Tour_, taking place in the main race courses with additional pathways and areas opened up compared to their regular counterparts in order to be designed akin to older battle courses. [DK Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/DK_Pass "DK Pass") and [Dino Dino Jungle](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dino_Dino_Jungle "Dino Dino Jungle") instead take place on routes near their racing counterparts, and, alongside Big Donut and Chain Chomp Desert, also appear on the world map and are driven across during Grand Prix, marking the first time battle courses appear in a Grand Prix, though they are only driven across briefly. Rather than sharing their music with their racing counterparts, all of the battle courses use arrangements of battle themes from past games: [Mario Bros. Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Bros._Circuit "Mario Bros. Circuit") uses _[Super Mario Kart](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_Kart "Super Mario Kart")_'s battle theme; Big Donut, Dino Dino Jungle, and DK Pass use their respective games' (_64_, _Double Dash!!_, and _DS_ respectively) battle themes; Moo Moo Meadows, [Salty Salty Speedway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Salty_Salty_Speedway "Salty Salty Speedway"), and Chain Chomp Desert respectively use Chain Chomp Wheel, [Delfino Pier](https://www.mariowiki.com/Delfino_Pier "Delfino Pier"), and Thwomp Desert's themes from _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_; and Peach Stadium uses [Battle Stadium](https://www.mariowiki.com/Battle_Stadium "Battle Stadium")'s theme from _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_. Items ----- A total of 27 items appear in _Mario Kart World_, 28 if including [Dash Food](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dash_Food "Dash Food"). As with _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_, items are automatically held behind racers in this game. Of the returning items, the Ice Flower and Hammer make their first appearance in a home console _Mario Kart_ game following their initial debut in _Mario Kart Tour_. The Mega Mushroom also makes its first home console appearance since its debut in _Mario Kart Wii_. Additionally, the Feather is now usable during races like in _Super Mario Kart_, rather than being exclusive to the [Battle](https://www.mariowiki.com/Battle "Battle") mode like in _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_ and _Mario Kart Tour_. _Mario Kart World_ has 227 newly arranged music tracks that can be listened to on the main menu, in Free Roam, or during [routes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Route "Route") in Grand Prix or VS Race; they consist of 108 arrangements from the _[Mario Kart](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart "Mario Kart")_ series, 103 from the [_Super Mario_](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(series/) "Super Mario (series)") series, 10 from the [_Yoshi_](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi_/(series/) "Yoshi (series)") series, 2 from _[Mario Paint](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Paint "Mario Paint")_, and 1 each from _[Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario_Land:_Super_Mario_Land_3 "Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3")_, _[Donkey Kong Country](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong_Country "Donkey Kong Country")_, _[Luigi's Mansion](https://www.mariowiki.com/Luigi%27s_Mansion "Luigi's Mansion")_, _[WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!](https://www.mariowiki.com/WarioWare,_Inc.:_Mega_Microgame$! "WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!")_, and _[Flipnote Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flipnote_Studio "wikipedia:Flipnote Studio")_. This randomized selection of music was referred to as the "jukebox" in development. Routes in Grand Prix have three to five dedicated arrangements that usually fit the theme of the source and/or the destination. Routes in VS Race have a completely random list of arrangements that do not necessarily fit the theme of the route even if one used in Grand Prix is selected; all Grand Prix arrangements play in this mode, plus a few more exclusive ones. Most VS Race arrangements can play in Free Roam, along with a few calmer and slower paced arrangements exclusive to that mode. Some tracks also play in a certain order, usually matching one of a game's soundtrack, and feature longer intros than in VS Race. Additionally, certain arrangements incorporate the melodies of other themes at certain points, such as the "Underground BGM" arrangement from _Super Mario Bros. 2_ also including part of "Ground BGM", or "Mario Drawing Song" having a nod to "Jump Up, Super Star!" While the arrangements for the returning courses usually stay true to the lengths of the original tracks, the battle course themes take after these arrangements and include improvised additional sections, except they loop. The following list does not include arrangements of themes for classic race courses and battle courses present in the game. Deluxe") Update history -------------- This is a detailed list of updates _Mario Kart World_ has received since launch. The following changes were made: > Fixed Issues > > * Fixed an issue where, if a player disconnects and reconnects a controller, the game may not progress as normal. > * When this issue occurs, there are times when ghost data from Time Trials will be deleted without warning from "View Rankings." Differences from previous _Mario Kart_ games -------------------------------------------- ### Gameplay * Races now consist of 24 racers compared to the eight or 12 from previous games. * In races where the player travels along a [route](https://www.mariowiki.com/Route "Route"), including Knockout Tour, racers will automatically begin moving before the starting countdown, though [Rocket Starts](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rocket_Start "Rocket Start") can still be performed. * Getting hit by a car or train at certain angles causes the player to become unbalanced as opposed to spinning out. * Rather than using hang-gliders like in games since _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_, vehicles now use retractable wings to glide. * Several changes made in _Mario Kart 8_ have been reverted back: * [Lakitu](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lakitu_/(Mario_Kart_referee/) "Lakitu (Mario Kart referee)") has mostly been reverted to his pre–_Mario Kart 8_ behavior, where instead of immediately picking up a racer who falls off of a course, the screen will briefly fade to black before fading back in to him dropping the racer. However, Lakitu does appear briefly before the screen fades. * Players can once again receive a speed boost when being dropped off by Lakitu by pressing the drive button before hitting the ground when Lakitu drops them. * Falling off the course causes the player to lose their items. * Players can no longer see the items of other players (unless they are defensive items or Mushrooms). * If a racer falls off a course in the middle of a gliding section, Lakitu will place them back in the air so they continue gliding rather than bringing them to the nearest road. * Vehicles no longer [drive underwater](https://www.mariowiki.com/Underwater_driving "Underwater driving"), and instead continue along the surface of the water. * The traction stat is no longer visible on the vehicle selection screen. * Unlike in _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_, the [Mini-Turbo](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mini-Turbo "Mini-Turbo") boost charge thresholds when drifting are once again identical across all character and vehicle combinations, like they were in _Mario Kart Wii_, _Mario Kart 7_ and the Wii U version of _Mario Kart 8_. * The functionally distinct [sport bike](https://www.mariowiki.com/Sport_bike_/(vehicle_class/) "Sport bike (vehicle class)") vehicle class that existed in _Mario Kart Wii_ and _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_ has been removed entirely. All bikes, regardless of their appearance or the rider's posture when riding them, are essentially considered to be [standard bikes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Standard_bike_/(vehicle_class/) "Standard bike (vehicle class)"), with the same drifting mechanics as all other vehicle types in the game. * The amount of coins a player can hold now caps off at 20, compared to the previous 10. * [Jump Boosting](https://www.mariowiki.com/Jump_Boost "Jump Boost") has been made more versatile: * It can now be performed multiple times in the air. * It can be performed at any time while gliding; tricking to the left or right will cause the racer to do a barrel roll. * It is now possible to trick off of other racers or obstacles by landing on top of them. * Racers can now charge up a [Charge Jump](https://www.mariowiki.com/Charge_Jump "Charge Jump"), allowing them to gain additional height, perform tricks, and gain speed boosts. * [Goombas](https://www.mariowiki.com/Goomba "Goomba") now charge towards racers when noticing them (similar to the 3D _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_/(series/) "Super Mario (series)")_ games), rather than simply walking in place or in a left-to-right pattern. * Explosions on the surface of water will create waves, which characters can trick off of. ### Controls ### Courses * Cups in Grand Prix are now based more on their region within the game's world map rather than following an overall difficulty progression across the game. * Unlike games since _[Mario Kart DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_DS "Mario Kart DS")_, no race or battle courses from _[Mario Kart: Super Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart:_Super_Circuit "Mario Kart: Super Circuit")_ return. ### Game Modes * By default, a Grand Prix now involves the first course of the cup being played with the multiple laps before subsequent races involve two-section routes leading into a full lap of a course for the final section. * In Time Trials, the game can be paused before the race starts. * VS Race and Battle mode options have several changes from _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_: * Teams can be set to No, Two, Three, or Four Teams instead of just No Teams or two teams with Team Game. * Items can only be set to Normal, Frantic, Mushrooms Only (as of version 1.2.0 and only for VS Race), or Custom Items (as of version 1.4.0). Shells Only, Bananas Only, Bob-ombs Only, No Items, No Items or Coins, and Skilled Items are no longer available. * Unlike in _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_, turning off every item in Custom Items in VS Race will no longer cause the Mushroom to automatically turn on. However, this does still occur in Battle mode. * COM Difficulty can be set to No COM in single player VS Race (as of version 1.2.0). * Setting COM Vehicles (between All Vehicles, Karts Only, or Bikes Only) is no longer available. * The "Choose" option in Course Selection has been renamed to "Open". * "In Order" is no longer available as a Course Selection option in VS Race and Battle mode. * VS Race's Race Count can be set to 3 (like _Mario Kart DS_, _Mario Kart Wii_, and the original _Mario Kart 8_) and 5 Races (like _Mario Kart DS_ and _Mario Kart Wii_), along with 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, and 32 Races still available. 24 and 48 Races are no longer available. * Battle mode's Round Count can be set to 3 Rounds (like the original _Mario Kart 8_), as well as 5 Rounds, along with 4, 6 and 8 Rounds still available. 10, 12, 15, 16, 20, 24, and 25 Rounds are no longer available. * Battle mode's Round Time is always 3 Minutes. Setting the Round Time from 1-5 Minutes is no longer available. * There is no longer a play stats menu. ### Items * [Mega Mushroom](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mega_Mushroom "Mega Mushroom"): * Racers under the effect of the Mega Mushroom item no longer shrink back to normal size when hit by Lightning. * After using a Mega Mushroom, the item slot shows the remaining time to be under the effect. As a result, the Mega Mushroom will count as being in use, so the player cannot use their other item nor receive another item if they already have two items, unlike in previous games where using the Mega Mushroom would remove it from the player's inventory immediately. * Like in _Mario Kart Tour_, the Mega Mushroom's theme from _[New Super Mario Bros.](https://www.mariowiki.com/New_Super_Mario_Bros. "New Super Mario Bros.")_ does not play while the item is in effect. * [Feather](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cape_Feather "Cape Feather"): * The Feather is now available in races, rather than being exclusive to Battle Mode. * Using the Feather item now allows racers to jump much higher and perform tricks after using it. * Feathers can now be dropped on the ground. * The player does not gain a speed boost upon landing after using a Feather unless they perform a trick after using it. * [Super Horn](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Horn "Super Horn"): * The Super Horn sound effect is identical across all characters, rather than being character-specific. * The Super Horn now stays in the item slot until it is fully used up. * [Star](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Star "Super Star"): * Stars can be found bouncing along the ground, as they do in the 2D _Super Mario_ games, in Free Roam. If a Star is dropped during a race, it will remain stationary, however. * A sound effect now plays indicating that the Star's effect is about to run out, similar to the mainline _Super Mario_ games. * [Lightning](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lightning "Lightning"): * The Lightning now only shocks players ahead of the user, rather than all opponents. * The Lightning now causes most players to be shrunk for the same amount of time, with racers in higher positions sequentially returning to their original size, similar to how it affected players prior to _[Mario Kart DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_DS "Mario Kart DS")_. * The Lightning stuns players for longer when it first strikes, with each character having a unique animation for being struck. * Being under the effects of a Lightning does not cause the music to distort, similar to games prior to _Mario Kart DS_. * [Spiny Shell](https://www.mariowiki.com/Spiny_Shell_/(blue/) "Spiny Shell (blue)"): * The Spiny Shell now launches racers into the air at a higher angle, similar to its effect from _Mario Kart: Double Dash!!_ to _Mario Kart Wii_. * Throwing the Spiny Shell has a slightly longer animation than throwing other items. * [Bullet Bill](https://www.mariowiki.com/Bullet_Bill "Bullet Bill"): * The Bullet Bill no longer causes players that it hits to spin out, instead causing them to get bumped out of the way and become unbalanced. * The Bullet Bill travels slower than before. * [Boo](https://www.mariowiki.com/Boo "Boo"): * The Boo item now applies a dithered transparency effect onto the user rather than turning them invisible, which is also applied to their held item resulting in them being invulnerable. * When using the Boo item, the user can now drive through off-road without slowing down, reverting to its behavior in _Mario Kart DS_. * When the Boo item steals from the player, like in _Mario Kart DS_, the Boo will hold the stolen item before leaving. When stealing the triple items, he will only hold one of the items. * When the Boo is in effect, the music and sound effects will be muffled. * [Fire Flower](https://www.mariowiki.com/Fire_Flower "Fire Flower"): * The Fire Flower now has a limit of eight fireballs, compared to the previous 10 in _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_7 "Mario Kart 7")_ and _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8 "Mario Kart 8")_. * [Boomerang Flower](https://www.mariowiki.com/Boomerang_Flower "Boomerang Flower"): * The Boomerang Flower now has a time limit when using it and does not leave the item slot until it is fully used up, similar to the Fire Flower. This allows for it to be used up to four times, compared to the previous three in _Mario Kart 8_. * Items now float on the surface of water, rather than sinking. * Moving the camera with the right stick will aim items in that direction, with a full range of 360 degrees. * Due to 1st place being able to hold a ? Block and Coin at the same time (as of version 1.2.0), 1st place is no longer guaranteed to get at least one defensive item with Normal item rules when the maximum item slots are filled (outside of online rooms with high lag), like _Mario Kart 8_ for the Wii U, and unlike _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_ and _Mario Kart Tour_ (when using three item slots). ### Aesthetic * Opening cinematics before races in the Grand Prix mode now show all of the courses at once before the first race, rather than each track individually at the start of each race. * The color of the sparks when charging an Ultra Mini-Turbo has been changed from purple to rainbow, similar to _[Mario Kart Arcade GP DX](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Arcade_GP_DX "Mario Kart Arcade GP DX")_. * Racers assume a horrified expression when they are about to be hit by a Spiny Shell. * Racers now brace themselves when tumbling, though they will still flail when spinning out. * The drivers of car obstacles are now visible. * The right stick can freely rotate characters and vehicles in the character and vehicle selection menu. Rotating in the vehicle selection menu will stop its automatic rotation. * The right stick can rotate cup trophies in the opposite direction of their automatic rotation. * Rather than being character-specific like in _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_, vehicle horns are now vehicle-specific. * Vehicles' horns cannot be used after a race ends. * Vehicles briefly swerve left and right after spinning out. * A sound effect does not play when the player changes placement, similar to games prior to _Mario Kart Wii_. * Similar to _Mario Kart Tour_, a graphic appears on screen indicating that the player has either hit an opponent or has been hit during Battle mode. ### Music * The sped-up version of a course's theme during the final lap is only used when playing the course without routes in either Grand Prix or VS Race. In Knockout Tour, the sped-up version is also used for the final race. * Frontrunning beats do not play when the player is in first. * When approaching a course from a route, a simple transitional version of its theme can be heard before the main theme starts playing upon crossing the finish line. Staff ----- _Main article: [List of Mario Kart World staff](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Mario_Kart_World_staff "List of Mario Kart World staff")_ _Mario Kart World_ is primarily developed by Nintendo EPD, with Kosuke Yabuki, Kenta Sato, Masaki Ishikawa, Shintaro Jikumaru, and Atsuko Asahi all returning from their respective roles from _ARMS_, another game led by the same team. In addition to Bandai Namco Studios returning to contribute to development, Monolith Soft and 1-Up Studio were also involved in the game's development. This game features neither [Shigeru Miyamoto](https://www.mariowiki.com/Shigeru_Miyamoto "Shigeru Miyamoto") nor series creator [Hideki Konno](https://www.mariowiki.com/Hideki_Konno "Hideki Konno") in lead development roles; only Konno receives a Special Thanks credit in the game. This is the first _Super Mario_ game to feature [Courtney Lin](https://www.mariowiki.com/Courtney_Lin "Courtney Lin") as the voices of [Peach](https://www.mariowiki.com/Peach "Peach") and [Baby Peach](https://www.mariowiki.com/Baby_Peach "Baby Peach"), [Laila Berzins](https://www.mariowiki.com/Laila_Berzins "Laila Berzins") and [Paul Castro Jr.](https://www.mariowiki.com/Paul_Castro_Jr. "Paul Castro Jr.") as the playable and non-playable [Toads](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad "Toad") respectively,[\[64\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-64) and [Laura Stahl](https://www.mariowiki.com/Laura_Stahl "Laura Stahl") as [Toadette](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toadette "Toadette"), following Nintendo's decision to recast their longtime voice actress, [Samantha Kelly](https://www.mariowiki.com/Samantha_Kelly "Samantha Kelly"). It is also the first game where [Kōji Takeda](https://www.mariowiki.com/K%C5%8Dji_Takeda "Kōji Takeda") replaces [Takashi Nagasako](https://www.mariowiki.com/Takashi_Nagasako "Takashi Nagasako") as the voice of Donkey Kong, reprising his role from the Japanese dub of _[The Super Mario Bros. Movie](https://www.mariowiki.com/The_Super_Mario_Bros._Movie "The Super Mario Bros. Movie")_, as well as the first game in the _Mario Kart_ series to feature [Kevin Afghani](https://www.mariowiki.com/Kevin_Afghani "Kevin Afghani"), [Giselle Fernandez](https://www.mariowiki.com/Giselle_Fernandez "Giselle Fernandez"), and [Dawn M. Bennett](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dawn_M._Bennett "Dawn M. Bennett") as the voices of their respective characters. Development ----------- "Mario Kart 9" redirects here. For the ninth _Mario Kart_ game released by Nintendo, excluding re-releases, see [Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_Tour "Mario Kart Tour"). [![Image 646: Image of Mario from an early build of Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/e/e7/MKWorld_Early_Mario.png/220px-MKWorld_Early_Mario.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Early_Mario.png) Promotional prerelease art for Mario and the Standard Kart Prototyping for _Mario Kart World_ started in March 2017, with official work on the game beginning at the end of the year following the release of _[ARMS](https://armswiki.org/wiki/ARMS_/(game/) "armswiki:ARMS (game)")_, another game created by the same development team. The game was originally being developed for the [Nintendo Switch](https://www.mariowiki.com/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch"),[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart1-1) but it was moved to the Nintendo Switch 2 around 2020 following the conception of the _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe_%E2%80%93_Booster_Course_Pass "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass")_.[\[65\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart2-65) _Mario Kart World_ is the first _Super Mario_ game since _[Super Paper Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Paper_Mario "Super Paper Mario")_ to be known to have been pushed back to a successor console. According to developers, had the game only introduced new courses and no new gimmicks, it would have likely been called _Mario Kart 9_; however, the open world gameplay was decided from the beginning, with the name _Mario Kart World_ already chosen very early in development.[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart1-1) [![Image 647: Concept artwork featuring Cow for Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/7/7c/MKWorld_Cow_Concept_Artwork_1.png/220px-MKWorld_Cow_Concept_Artwork_1.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Cow_Concept_Artwork_1.png) A sketch of [Cow](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") driving a truck, which the producers enjoyed The decision to include [Cow](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow "Cow") as a playable character originated from a sketch done by one of the artists, featuring Cow driving a blue truck. The producers were so amused by the image that Cow was soon added as a playable character, which the developers named one of the "NPC drivers". Other obstacles soon became "NPC drivers" following Cow's addition, such as [Pokey](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pokey "Pokey").[\[52\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart3-52) The decision to increase the racer count to 24 came from one of the developers thinking that 12-player races would feel empty once the racers became spread out.[\[1\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-InterviewPart1-1) Glitches -------- ### Stuck Bomber Bill [![Image 648: A shrunken Bomber Bill seen in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/9/96/MKWorld_Bomber_Bill_Glitch.png/200px-MKWorld_Bomber_Bill_Glitch.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_Bomber_Bill_Glitch.png) The shrunken [Bomber Bill](https://www.mariowiki.com/Bomber_Bill "Bomber Bill") on the left side of the road, shortly before disappearing If a [Banzai Bill Cannon](https://www.mariowiki.com/Banzai_Bill_Cannon "Banzai Bill Cannon") carried by a [pickup truck](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pickup_truck "Pickup truck") shoots a [Bomber Bill](https://www.mariowiki.com/Bomber_Bill "Bomber Bill") inside of a [Knockout Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#Knockout_Tour "Mario Kart World") checkpoint, the Bomber Bill will briefly become stuck inside the checkpoint before disappearing. In this state, the Bomber Bill remains shrunken down as if it were still inside the cannon.[\[66\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-SirloinKnockout-66) ### Out-of-bounds shortcut In online races on [Whistlestop Summit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Whistlestop_Summit "Whistlestop Summit") and [Dandelion Depths](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dandelion_Depths "Dandelion Depths"), players can abuse the fact that [Lakitu](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lakitu_/(Mario_Kart_referee/) "Lakitu (Mario Kart referee)") will not pick up their COM-controlled character immediately after leaving a room.[\[67\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-67) On Whistlestop Summit, if a player jumps off to the right on the yellow rail after the long bridge and leaves the race before getting picked up by Lakitu, he will not pick up the COM-controlled character that races in place of the player, causing it to skip to the path below. On Dandelion Depths, if a player jumps off to the left of the road in the spiral turn and leaves the race before getting picked up by Lakitu, he will also not pick up the COM-controlled character that races in place of the player, causing it to skip to the end of the course's water section. If the glitch is done on the final lap, it will cause them a near guaranteed win unless first place is too close to the place where they end up after the shortcut. This is only useful in online lobbies during the last race due to the player's score resetting when they rejoin. ### Disabled Lakitu [![Image 649: A demonstration of the disabled Lakitu glitch in effect on the Rainbow Road track in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/8/85/MKWorld_DisabledLakitu.jpg/300px-MKWorld_DisabledLakitu.jpg)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWorld_DisabledLakitu.jpg) [Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario "Mario") exploring an out-of-bounds area in [Rainbow Road](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rainbow_Road_/(Mario_Kart_World/) "Rainbow Road (Mario Kart World)"). Note [Lakitu](https://www.mariowiki.com/Lakitu "Lakitu") attempting to pick up Mario; this animation would play continuously while the glitch was active. In VS Race or Time Trials, if the player selected any course, plugged in a single Joy-Con or Joy-Con 2 controller at the "OK" screen, and started the race or time trial with precise timing before the controller screen appeared, they would load into the course with the UI and race start timer sound effects missing. In this state, if the player entered an out-of-bounds area or fell off the course, they would not be picked up by Lakitu despite having the out-of-bounds animation play. This allowed the player to freely explore a glitched version of the game's map which lacked most objects and had non-functional [Warp Pipes](https://www.mariowiki.com/Warp_Pipe "Warp Pipe"). The player could exit this state by pausing the game, entering [Photo Mode](https://www.mariowiki.com/Photo_Mode "Photo Mode"), or swapping controllers. If the glitch was done on Rainbow Road, the course would be unloaded once the player respawned if they fell off it.[\[68\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-68) After ten minutes, the race or time trial is forced to end; if the Lakitu glitch was still active at this point, all menu options would cause the game to be unresponsive, forcing the player to close it via the HOME Menu. This could be avoided by disconnecting a controller before selecting a menu option. This glitch was fixed in the [version 1.4.1](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#Ver._1.4.1 "Mario Kart World") patch, released on December 15, 2025. Reception --------- _Mario Kart World_ received generally positive reviews. The departure from the traditional formula was praised, but certain aspects were considered shortcomings of the result of that direction. | Reviews | | --- | | Reviewer, publication | Score | Comment | | Scott Duwe, [Destructoid](https://www.destructoid.com/reviews/mario-kart-world-review/) | 9/10 | "_Mario Kart World is the latest and potentially greatest in the long-running arcade racer franchise, brought to the next level with the Nintendo Switch 2's hardware and an expansive roster of racers, tracks, and endless fun to be had. ._" | | Steve Watts, [GameSpot](https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/mario-kart-world-review/1900-6418371/) | 9/10 | "_Mario Kart World is a massive, sprawling sequel that playfully expands and iterates on the qualities that made Mario Kart 8 Deluxe such an enduring success. It's an incredibly fun and rewarding kart racing experience that's easy to understand, with enough mechanical nuance to reward veteran kart racers, all presented beautifully as a Switch 2 showpiece._" | | Logan Plant, [IGN](https://www.ign.com/articles/mario-kart-world-review) | 8/10 | "_Mario Kart World may not make the most convincing case that going open-world was the boost the series needed, but excellent multiplayer racing, incredible polish, and the thrilling new Knockout Tour mode still more than live up to its legacy._" | | Aggregators | | Compiler | Score | | Metacritic | [86](https://www.metacritic.com/game/switch/mario-kart-world) | ### Sales By June 30, 2025, _Mario Kart World_ had sold 5.63 million units worldwide, immediately becoming the best-selling game for the Nintendo Switch 2.[\[69\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-69) This meant the game had a 96% attach rate with sales of the Nintendo Switch 2 in the console's first month of availability. As of September 30, 2025, the game had sold 9.57 million units.[\[70\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-70) ### Awards and acknowledgements _Mario Kart World_ was nominated for two awards at [The Game Awards 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2025 "wikipedia:The Game Awards 2025"), in the categories "Best Family Game" and "Best Sports/Racing Game".[\[71\]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Kart_World#cite_note-71) The game would go on to win "Best Sports/Racing Game", while _[Donkey Kong Bananza](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong_Bananza "Donkey Kong Bananza")_ won "Best Family Game" instead. It was also one of 30 games selected for the "Player's Choice" award, but failed to receive enough votes to make the top 10.  Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://annual.wikimedia.org/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

34% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

11% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts
